If only I gave a shit about /v/Sports

edit: inb4 this post is labeled a brigade post

Step 1: The Bait

Usually, you will have to find something to be "concerned" about, but an experienced concern troll can often create good situations out of there being nothing to be concerned about.

I know full well that kevdude has just been appointed to /v/Sports to clean up spam. Looking at the rules, I can see Rule #5 is a pretty grey area rule: "Keep your submissions on topic. This is sports. Unrelated links will be removed."

Of course, this by default means that any Meta posts need to be deleted, as they aren't related to sports at all, so I make This low effort post as I know it will be removed, but it is still pretty stupid to remove Meta posts, so I have some leverage. More importantly, I have something to be concerned about.

Step 2: The Accusation

My post has been removed by kevdude, and now I have to complain about it. I start off with a pretty shitty argument: "How is this off topic? It is a meta post about the state of the sub". This plants the seed for later concern to be had.

Kevdude thinks this post is a "shitpost", which it is. What I need to do is convince him that I am legitimately concerned. To do this, I need to pretend I am trying to do something good for the sub: "Rather than removing my post and saying it's a shitpost, is it not better to actually engage in conversation with other people over what to do about it?"

Here comes the accusation: "Could it possibly be that you're removing my submission because of who I am rather than what I was saying?". Whether or not this is true, it's going to force him to hit back a little: "Could it be that you are ignoring that to stir shit? Look, I don't give a fuck about "power". If you want to shit up v/sports I would sooner step down than allow my presence to create a shitshow for this sub."

Step 3: Legitimising Your Concern

After I have been accused of drama stirring, I can play the victim. This is the most important step, and there are a couple of ways to do this well.

The method I employ in my comment is a pincer attack of "I'm trying to do something good for the sub/I am on your side and providing sources". These sources are of course complete BS, a mod is always going to have to make Meta posts.

Result:
